newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chip shares jump after bullish US chip data.
newsitem.headline: Japan chip shares jump after bullish US chip data.

text.p: Shares in the Japanese semiconductor sector rose on Tuesday morning, helped by bullish U.S. computer chip data, traders said.
The U.S. semiconductor book-to-bill ratio rose to 1.10 in October from a revised 0.98 in September.
The share price of Advantest Corp had jumped 60 yen to 4,360 yen by 0048 GMT, on volume of 31,800 shares.
Shares of some major chip firms saw heavy trade in the first section.
NEC Corp was up 10 yen at 1,310 yen at 0053 GMT. Turnover was 2.193 million shares, the second heaviest.
Toshiba Corp was up 10 yen to 742 yen at 0111 GMT, in a turnover of 1.729 million shares.
Fujitsu Ltd was unchanged at 1,020 yen after earlier inching up to 1,030 yen.

"The (ratio's) rise to 1.10 in October for the first time in ten months, as well as the increase in new orders, is providing support to the shares," said Akishige Ishikura, an analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
The index, widely regarded as a sign of the computer industry's health, means that manufacturers received $110 in new orders for every $100 in shipments.
New orders jumped 17.9 percent in October from the previous month.
